_banner: vocabulary.json -- everything that turns SOUND into CANONICAL TEXT.
Two things live here and nothing else: the whisper initial prompt, and the
spoken-to-canonical alias table. What happens to the text AFTERWARDS is
commands.json's job. The split is not tidiness: the prompt and the aliases are
the two halves of one measured trade-off and they have to be read together,
while the command registry changes for completely unrelated reasons (a new
driver, a new flag) and would otherwise drag this file along with it.
THE PROMPT IS PROSE AND THE SPOKEN FORMS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN IT.
whisper's initial prompt is conditioning TRANSCRIPT TEXT, not a vocabulary
list, and it imitates whatever style it is handed. Both halves measured on
identical audio at temperature 0, so this reproduces and will never look like
flakiness:
comma-separated keyword list -> 'Run the D3Q27, K8, gamma, 100 with tau1.'
it DELETED 'colour gradient case'
the same vocabulary as prose -> 'Run the D3Q27 colour gradient case at
gamma one hundred with tau one.'  (exact)
And putting the spoken forms in the prompt BACKFIRES for the same reason: with
'dee two queue nine' in the prompt whisper emitted the literal `dee two queue
nine`; with that one clause removed and nothing else changed, it emitted
`D2Q9`. So `whisper_prompt` below contains ONLY canonical forms, and every
spoken form is in `aliases`, applied AFTER transcription.
WHAT THE PROMPT ACTUALLY BUYS IS NARROWER THAN EXPECTED. tiny.en already gets
D3Q27 right with no prompt at all, so the premise that a lattice name needed
help was wrong. What it fixes is Orszag-Tang (from 'Orces Actang'),
Rayleigh-Benard (from 'Rayleigh Bernard'), Poiseuille (from 'Poisell'),
Esoteric Pull (from 'esoteric cool'), Kokkos (from 'caucus') and the British
'colour'.
AND THE PROMPT IS NOT SUFFICIENT, WHICH IS WHY THE ALIAS TABLE EXISTS. The same
sentence, the same model, the same prompt, differing only in the room noise
spliced around it, transcribed once as `ctest` and once as `ptest`. One run
would have 'proved' the prompt fixed it. Two runs show the prompt shifts the
odds and the alias table is what closes them, so the entries for ctest and for
tau are load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO. It does not decide anything: no entry here routes,
runs or refuses. D3Q19 maps to the canonical `D3Q19` precisely so that the
refusal in commands.json can SEE it -- deleting the alias would make a stale
spoken command silently mean nothing instead of being refused out loud. It also
carries no spoken numbers beyond the handful of exponents below: whisper writes
digits correctly and a general number parser would be a second grammar to keep
in step with the drivers.
Alias matching is longest-first, case-insensitive, on word boundaries, with
[\s,\-]+ between words because whisper punctuates freely. So a short rule
cannot eat the head of a long one and 'D3Q27, K8' still matches.
whisper_prompt: We are working on M3LB, a lattice Boltzmann solver written in C++ on Kokkos. The lattices are D2Q9, D2Q5, D3Q7 and D3Q27, and the collision operators are BGK, TRT, MRT, central moments, the colour gradient and the conservative Allen-Cahn phase field. I build with CMake in Release and run ctest. The cases are Poiseuille, Taylor-Green, Orszag-Tang, Rayleigh-Benard, Hartmann, Shercliff, the lid-driven cavity, natural convection, the static droplet, Laplace's law, EHD electroconvection, the free surface, the urban plume and the aorta. I read off the Reynolds, Rayleigh, Prandtl, Nusselt, Hartmann and Mach numbers, tau and omega, the relaxation rate, the density ratio, the spurious current, the interface width, Boussinesq buoyancy, bounce-back and specular walls, Esoteric Pull, shifted populations, FP32 and FP64, and whether the run says PASS or FAIL. I also ask for git status and git log, for the branch and what is uncommitted, and for the frame check script.

prompt_rules.why_not_a_list: A comma-separated keyword list measurably destroys the transcript: it deleted 'colour gradient case' and injected commas. The prompt is conditioning text, so it teaches output style.
prompt_rules.no_spoken_forms: Spoken forms in the prompt make whisper emit them verbatim. They belong in `aliases`, applied after transcription.
prompt_rules.length_note: 150 words and 968 characters, counted from this file rather than asserted -- the figure this text arrived with was 142, which was wrong, and it was 128 before the tooling sentence was added. `python3 -c "import json;p=json.load(open('voice/vocabulary.json'))['whisper_prompt'];print(len(p.split()), len(p))"` is the check, and it must be re-run after any edit to the prompt.
prompt_rules.ceiling: whisper-cli documents the initial prompt ceiling as n_text_ctx/2 tokens; 150 words is roughly 200 and is comfortably inside it.
prompt_rules.tooling_sentence: The last sentence names git, the branch and the frame check. It was added because the prompt described the PHYSICS and nothing the user actually types: synthesised 'jarvis git status' came back from tiny.en as 'Jarvis Gibbs status.' -- routed to the agent instead of to the git_status entry, and 'Gibbs' is a plausible physics word, so the old prompt may have been actively favouring it. It is PROSE, like the rest, for the reason recorded above.

_silence_hallucinations_why: WHISPER DOES NOT RETURN NOTHING FOR SILENCE. IT RETURNS A SENTENCE, AND IT
RETURNS THE SAME ONE EVERY TIME. Measured: 8 s of genuine room silence
(mean -46.8 dB, max -31.0 dB) POSTed to tiny.en returned the first entry
below on 3/3 runs with the bias prompt and 1/1 without it. In the first
live daemon run a variant arrived as 'Jarvis has a letter along the
sentence so that the rendering takes a measurable amount of time...' --
wake_match scored it 1.0, hit=True, and jarvis built a full claude argv out
of room noise. jarvis.py's _ANNOTATION_RE cannot see this: it strips
[BLANK_AUDIO] and *laughs* by FORM, and free prose has no form.
THIS LIST IS THE SECOND DEFENCE, NOT THE FIRST. The first is acoustic and
lives in handle_segment(): a segment must carry MIN_SEG_MS of frames that
the VAD found above the adapted floor before it is transcribed at all. A
denylist can only ever catch the hallucinations already observed, so grow
it from voice/logs/*.jsonl -- every rejection is logged with its
similarity, and the match is difflib at 0.9, not equality, because the
silence_hallucinations: This is a deliberately long-sentence so that the rendering takes a measurable amount of time.
Jarvis has a letter along the sentence so that the rendering takes a measurable amount of time.

aliases.why: Safety net only. whisper gets the lattice names right unprompted more often than not.
cs2 is 1/4 here, not 1/3. The alias only fixes the name; the arithmetic trap is CLAUDE.md's.

tiny.en CANNOT say ctest: measured 'ptest' twice. Bare 'test' is deliberately NOT here -- it would rewrite 'run the fast tests' into 'run the fast ctests', and the repo really does have both meanings.
tiny.en hears tau as 'that he are you'. Measured, and load-bearing: tau is how this user reads the stability floor.
The Ra at which rb_high_ra diverges by t/t_ff ~ 30. Recognising it is what lets the registry refuse the bare default.
